title: Keys and Efficient List Updates
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of Keys and Efficient List Updates in a Vue 3 application.
Apply at least one of the syllabus subtopics in a small, inspectable example.
Verify one expected behavior and identify a relevant edge case.

content.intro: This lesson studies Keys and Efficient List Updates within Vue Template Syntax. The source PDF subtopics are preserved below and connected to an original working-style example.
content.why_it_matters: Templates keep intent visible: the UI describes what should appear for the current state instead of manually editing the DOM.

content_blocks.title: Keys and Efficient List Updates: Component communication
content_blocks.alt_text: Component communication diagram for lesson 22: Keys and Efficient List Updates. Parent owns the value or business intent → Child receives data and renders its view → Child emits intent; parent decides updates
content_blocks.caption: Component flow: data moves into children through props; emitted events communicate requested changes back to the owner.

content_blocks.title: The idea in context
content_blocks.text: Vue templates bind readable HTML-like markup to data and events, using expressions and directives for dynamic behavior. This lesson focuses on Keys and Efficient List Updates. Start by naming the state, component, browser behavior, or deployment boundary involved; then predict what should change and test the smallest example.

items.title: Purpose of the key attribute
items.text: For Purpose of the key attribute, document what data enters the component, which events leave it, and where shared content or behavior belongs. Keep props one-way, emit changes rather than mutating parent-owned values, and add slots only when a real composition point is needed.

items.title: Stable and unique keys
items.text: For Stable and unique keys, express the intended DOM result through a Vue template binding instead of directly manipulating the DOM. Keep template expressions small, use stable keys for stateful list items, and choose directives based on whether content should be created, removed, or merely hidden.

items.title: Keys when rendering components
items.text: For Keys when rendering components, document what data enters the component, which events leave it, and where shared content or behavior belongs. Keep props one-way, emit changes rather than mutating parent-owned values, and add slots only when a real composition point is needed.

content_blocks.text: Extend the example to include “Stable and unique keys”. Keep the same behavior for the ordinary input, then try an empty, invalid, repeated, or failure condition that makes sense for the example. Record the expected result before testing.

items.title: Assuming behavior instead of checking it
items.text: Write down the expected result and reproduce the issue in the smallest possible example; inspect the browser Console and the exact reactive value or request.

items.title: Ignoring an edge case
items.text: Try empty input, a missing item, repeated interaction, a failed request, or unmounting while work is pending; handle the case explicitly.

items.title: Putting every responsibility in one component
items.text: Separate display, reusable logic, API service, and shared state when that boundary makes the behavior easier to test and explain.

content_blocks.text: Use semantic HTML, readable labels, keyboard-operable controls, and visible errors where the example interacts with users. content.task: Create a small example for “Keys and Efficient List Updates” that applies “Purpose of the key attribute”, predicts the expected result, and verifies a relevant boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named Vue concept rather than only mentioning it.
The expected output or observable behavior is written down and can be checked locally.
At least one boundary, loading, invalid-input, or failure case is tested or explicitly reasoned about.
The example uses semantic/accessible interaction patterns and does not treat frontend state as authoritative security.
hints: Start with the smallest observable part of “Purpose of the key attribute”.

common_mistakes.problem: The example only covers the happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Real interfaces receive empty values, delayed responses, invalid input, and failed requests.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one realistic edge/failure case and state its expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: The code assumes an API or feature exists in every runtime.
common_mistakes.why: Tool and API support depends on Vue, the build tool, or the chosen SSR/test framework.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the linked official reference and record the runtime/version assumption.
